献给博夫

[P4] 一个晴朗寒冷的星期五，有个名叫阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦的宝宝，在德国古城乌尔姆诞生。那天是1879年3月14日。
呜呜……

[P5] 但是，新生儿只为这个家庭带来了短暂的喜悦。
奶奶发现：“他太胖了，太胖了！”
妈妈担心他的头太大，他的后脑勺有点肿。
不过医生说，别担心，这个孩子一切正常，他很好。

爱因斯坦渐渐长大，很快就到了牙牙学语的年龄，可是，他一句话也不会说，家人焦急地等了又等。他真的没有问题吗？
后来，他终于说话了，而且一开口就显出他的聪明。快3岁时，父母答应给他一个惊喜，他满心期待的是玩具，没想到竟然是个小妹妹。他说：“小妹妹身上怎么没有轮子？”

[P6] 爱因斯坦有时对妹妹玛雅很粗暴，他曾经差点儿把棒球扔到妹妹身上，还差一点用锄头打到她的头。后来玛雅说，爱因斯坦其实需要一个“坚固的骷髅”来当他的妹妹。

可怜的玛雅并不是爱因斯坦唯一发脾气的对象。有好几次，只要他不高兴，他的脸色和鼻尖就会发白，接着暴跳如雷。他的脾气实在太坏了，就连父母为他请的家庭教师也被吓得逃之夭夭。

[P7] 不过，爱因斯坦也不是一直在生气发呆，
对于感兴趣的事，他总是非常投入。
他很喜欢叠纸牌屋，而且可以叠到14层那么高。

父亲送他的简易指南针也让他着迷。他把指南针
翻来转去和抖着放，指针却永远指着南北方！他很好
奇：“里面到底有什么秘密？”

[P8] 后来，爱因斯坦全家搬到了大城市慕尼黑，父母为了鼓励他独立，特别准许4岁的他，在没家人的陪伴下自己上街。

[P9] 他开始上学了，可是在同学们的眼中，他是个
怪男孩。
男孩们都喜欢踢球，爱因斯坦却不喜欢运动。

[P10] 男孩们看见军人游行都很兴奋，爱因斯坦却觉得很不安。

[P11] 爱因斯坦是学生中唯一的犹太人，有些同学因此
嘲笑、咒骂和羞辱他。

在学校，只要是爱因斯坦喜欢的科目，他都学得很好，但是不
感兴趣的科目，他就懒得学。他喜欢数学，对拉丁文和希腊文却兴
趣平平。

老师在课堂提问时，爱因斯坦总是要想很久才回答，这点让老
师很不满意，因为他们喜欢清楚又快速的答案。后来，老师常看见
爱因斯坦嘴唇微张，喃喃自语……

爱因斯坦的智商有问题吗？老师们怀疑。

[P12] 然而，爱因斯坦的成绩非常好。
在家里，他努力练习小提琴，尤其是莫扎特的曲子，完全不需要老师督促。
“我相信，做一件事情，热情比责任感更重要——
至少，对我来说是如此。”他长大后这么说。
爱因斯坦12岁那年，父母邀请了一位名叫麦克斯·塔尔穆德的医学系学生来家里做客，他俩成了好朋友。对爱因斯坦来说，这是个很特别的体验，后来，他形容自己当时不再那么“孤独”了。
麦克斯给爱因斯坦一本几何学的书。那个充满形状、线条、顶点和角的世界，让爱因斯坦十分惊奇。
“才几个月，他就把书全部读懂了。”麦克斯说，
“他马上又投入到更高阶的数学研究……没多久，他的数学天赋一飞冲天，连我都追不上。”

[P13] 除了数学，其他的学校作业都让爱因斯坦觉得很无聊。
“那些漫不经心和机械式的教学真令人难受。”他说，“我宁可接受各种处罚，也不要学习枯燥乏味的东西。”
他对学校有些课程不感兴趣，态度冷漠，让一些老师对他存有偏见。
有位老师这么告诉爱因斯坦，“你这辈子绝对不可能有成就”。
爱因斯坦根本不在乎老师怎么说，整天沉浸在数学和音乐的世界里。他努力思考心中的疑惑：乘坐光束的感觉像什么？如果能够以惊人的光速前进，世界会不会变得不一样？

[P14] 爱因斯坦15岁时，因为父亲工作需要，全家必须搬到意大利的米兰。但是，就在爱因斯坦要离开德国时，得知法律规定他必须服兵役。于是，他被迫留下来，先完成高中学业再去当兵。爱因斯坦搬进了学生宿舍。
他的心情跌入了谷底，在学校过得一团糟，很渴望回到舒服的家。他的情绪和健康渐渐走下坡，为了帮助他康复，他获得特别许可，终于离开学校，去意大利与家人团聚。

那里的生活如同重见光明。爱因斯坦有了家人的陪伴，除了能参观博物馆，当然，还能继续钻研数学。因此，爱因斯坦开始发展他的所有爱好，就像儿时金纸牌屋一样。即使参加宴会，他也在解复杂难算的数学题，完全不理会周围宾客的谈话和音乐。

[P15] 他申请了去瑞士苏黎世理工学院学习，可是，由于没有准备那些在学校被他忽略的科目，他并没有通过入学考试。接着，他花了一整年取得了高中文凭，然后顺利进入理工学院继续学习。

毕业后他本想在大学谋个职位，可是没有机会。1902年，他接受瑞士专利局三级技术员的职位，那儿是个专门负责管理新发明的机构。

后来，爱因斯坦结了婚，还当了爸爸。

家庭和工作没有使他停止疑惑和思考——那些关于数学、光线、时间、世界和宇宙的各种问题。

偶尔，他推着婴儿车走过苏黎世的街道，脑中就像布满星星的夜空一样，充满各种闪闪发亮的幻想。如同星被人组合描绘成星座的图案，爱因斯坦脑海中那自由空间、时间、能量和物质所构成的图像，也逐渐成形，那是从来没有人见过的图像。

[P17] 爱因斯坦发现，光是由称为光子的细小微量所组成，然后形成光束，就像从水管喷出来的水柱。他说，所有东西都在活动，当某些东西动得像光一样快时，就会发生奇妙的事，例如时钟行进的速度仿佛变慢了，物体好像也变短了。爱因斯坦说，有些像沙粒一样小的东西，其实蕴含着难以想象的能量。
对科学家来说，爱因斯坦发现的就是光电效应、相对论和E=mc²。
对我们来说，他的想法就等于电动门、电视、太空漫游和原子弹。
对爱因斯坦来说，他的成就为自己赢得了诺贝尔奖。他变得非常有名，但是在他眼中，名声好像父母宴中的嘈杂与喧哗，他一点儿都不在乎，仍然醉心于思考发明中的各种难题。
对整个世界来说，爱因斯坦这个名字不再代表胖宝宝、爱生气的孩子或是怪男孩，而是一位伟大的思想家。

[P18] 作者的话

阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦已经在半个世纪前去世，然后，他著名的方程式
E=mc²却仍然影响着这个世界的思潮。除了名声，还有许多误解和误会，也
一路伴随着爱因斯坦。

E=mc²结合了物质和能量，可能是最广为人知的方程式，但是它并没有
为爱因斯坦赢得诺贝尔奖。1921年，诺贝尔奖颁给了爱因斯坦有关光的本质
的理论——《论运动物体的电动力学》，这个理论和E=mc²与《特殊相对论》
都完成于1905年。因此，那年也被称为爱因斯坦的奇迹年。不过，这道奇迹
并没有成为研究辅助经费与大学教授工资的保障，反而减少了他身为专利研
究员、父亲和丈夫的时间。

爱因斯坦没有发明原子弹。1939年，他曾写信告诉罗斯福总统，纳粹正
计划制造原子弹，并且建议美国增加研究原子弹的经费。事实上，那时当时
几乎不受重视的信，后来的确成为促成曼哈顿计划和美国制造原子弹的主
因。不过爱因斯坦完全没有参与其中。甚至因为他的社会上主张反战与和平主
义理念，被视为危险分子，并被严格地排除在这个计划之外。

1955年，阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦在新泽西州逝世。法医确认他死于心脏衰
竭，并取出爱因斯坦的大脑，保存在实验室超过40年之久。关于这颗大脑
的事被记载在迈克尔·帕蒂尔尼蒂著名的著作——《送爱因斯坦回家》中。

★ 2005年美国图书馆协会年度好书推荐

Dedicated to Boyu

[P4] On a clear, cold Friday, a baby named Albert Einstein was born in the ancient German city of Ulm. That day was March 14, 1879.
Wah-wah...

[P5] But the newborn only brought the family brief joy.
Grandma noticed: "He's too fat, too fat!"
Mom worried that his head was too big and his back of the head was a bit swollen.
But the doctor said, don't worry, the child is perfectly normal, he's fine.

Einstein gradually grew up and soon reached the age when children start to babble, yet he couldn't say a single word. The family anxiously waited and waited. Was there really something wrong with him?
Later, he finally began to speak, and right from the start, his intelligence showed. When he was nearly 3 years old, his parents promised him a surprise. He eagerly expected a toy, but to his surprise, it was a little sister. He said, "Why doesn't the little sister have wheels?"

[P6] Einstein was sometimes very rough with his sister Maya. He once almost threw a baseball at her and nearly hit her head with a shovel. Later, Maya said Einstein actually needed a "sturdy skull" to be his sister.

Poor Maya was not the only one Einstein took his temper out on. Several times, whenever he was unhappy, his face and nose would turn pale, and then he would jump up and down in rage. His temper was so bad that even the family tutor his parents hired was scared away.

[P7] However, Einstein wasn't always angry or daydreaming.
When he was interested in something, he was always deeply focused.
He really liked building card houses, and could build them as high as 14 layers.

The simple compass his father gave him also fascinated him. He turned it over and over, shook it, but the needle always pointed north and south! He was very curious: “What secret is inside?”

[P8] Later, the Einstein family moved to the big city of Munich. To encourage his independence, his parents specially allowed the 4-year-old to go out on the street without any family members accompanying him.

[P9] He started school, but in his classmates' eyes, he was a
strange boy.
The boys all liked playing soccer, but Einstein didn't like sports.

[P10] The boys were excited to see the military parade, but Einstein felt very uneasy.

[P11] Einstein was the only Jew among the students, and some classmates therefore
laughed at, cursed, and humiliated him.

At school, whenever it was a subject Einstein liked, he learned it well, but for
subjects he was not interested in, he was lazy to study. He liked math, but had
little interest in Latin and Greek.

When the teacher asked questions in class, Einstein always took a long time to
answer, which made the teacher dissatisfied, because they preferred clear and
quick answers. Later, the teacher often saw Einstein with his lips slightly open,
muttering to himself……

Did Einstein have an intelligence problem? The teachers doubted.

[P12] However, Einstein's grades were excellent.
At home, he practiced the violin diligently, especially Mozart's pieces, without needing any teacher's supervision.
"I believe that passion is more important than responsibility when doing something—
at least, that's true for me," he said later in life.
When Einstein was 12 years old, his parents invited a medical student named Max Talmud to their home. They became good friends. For Einstein, it was a special experience, and later he described himself as no longer feeling so "lonely".
Max gave Einstein a book on geometry. The world full of shapes, lines, vertices, and angles amazed Einstein.
"Within a few months, he had read the entire book," Max said,
"He immediately plunged into higher-level mathematical research... soon, his mathematical talent soared so high that I couldn't keep up."

[P13] Besides math, all other schoolwork bored Einstein.
"Those careless and mechanical teachings are truly unbearable," he said. "I'd rather accept any punishment than learn dull, boring things."
He showed little interest in some school subjects and was cold in attitude, causing some teachers to hold prejudice against him.
One teacher told Einstein, "You will never achieve anything in your life."
Einstein didn't care what the teacher said. He spent his days immersed in the worlds of math and music. He tried to think through his inner questions: What would it feel like to ride on a beam of light? If one could travel at an incredible speed of light, would the world be any different?

[P14] When Einstein was 15, because his father's job required it, the whole family had to move to Milan, Italy. However, just as Einstein was about to leave Germany, he learned that the law required him to serve in the military. So, he was forced to stay, finish high school first, and then go to serve. Einstein moved into a student dormitory.
His mood plunged to the bottom; he had a terrible time at school and longed to return to his comfortable home. His emotions and health gradually declined. To help him recover, he received special permission and finally left school to reunite with his family in Italy.

Life there was like seeing the light again. With his family by his side, Einstein could visit museums and, of course, continue studying mathematics. Thus, Einstein began to develop all his hobbies, just like building paper houses as a child. Even at parties, he was solving complex math problems, completely ignoring the conversations and music around him.

[P15] He applied to study at the Swiss Federal Polytechnic in Zurich, but failed the entrance exam because he hadn't prepared for the subjects he had ignored at school. He then spent a full year earning his high school diploma and successfully entered the Polytechnic to continue his studies.

After graduation, he hoped to get a position at a university, but there was no opportunity. In 1902, he accepted a position as a third-class technical assistant at the Swiss Patent Office, an institution dedicated to managing new inventions.

Later, Einstein got married and became a father.

Family and work did not stop him from questioning and thinking—about mathematics, light, time, the world, and the universe.

Occasionally, he pushed a baby carriage through the streets of Zurich, his mind like a star-filled night sky, full of sparkling, brilliant ideas. Just as stars are combined and drawn into constellations, the images in Einstein’s mind—of free space, time, energy, and matter—also gradually took shape. These were images no one had ever seen before.

[P17] Einstein discovered that light is made up of tiny particles called photons, which form beams, just like water coming out of a hose. He said that everything is in motion, and when something moves as fast as light,奇妙 things happen, such as clocks seeming to slow down and objects appearing to shorten. Einstein said that some tiny things, like grains of sand, actually contain unimaginable amounts of energy.
For scientists, Einstein's discoveries were the photoelectric effect, relativity, and E=mc².
For us, his ideas are equivalent to electric doors, televisions, space travel, and atomic bombs.
For Einstein himself, his achievements earned him the Nobel Prize. He became very famous, but in his eyes, fame was like the noise and commotion at a parents' party—he didn't care at all, and remained deeply engrossed in thinking about various problems in invention.
For the entire world, the name Einstein no longer represents a chubby baby, an angry child, or a strange boy, but a great thinker.

[P18] Author's Note

Albert Einstein passed away half a century ago, yet his famous equation
E=mc² continues to influence the world's thinking. Besides fame, there have been many misunderstandings and misconceptions that have accompanied Einstein all along.

E=mc² combines matter and energy and is perhaps the most widely known equation. However, it did not win Einstein the Nobel Prize. In 1921, the Nobel Prize was awarded to Einstein for his theory on the nature of light—"On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies." This theory, along with E=mc² and the Special Theory of Relativity, was completed in 1905. Thus, that year is also known as Einstein's miracle year. However, this miracle did not become a guarantee of research funding or university professor salaries; instead, it reduced the time he had as a patent researcher, father, and husband.

Einstein did not invent the atomic bomb. In 1939, he wrote a letter to President Roosevelt warning that the Nazis were planning to build atomic bombs and suggested increasing U.S. funding for atomic bomb research. In fact, this letter, which was largely ignored at the time, later became a key factor in launching the Manhattan Project and the U.S. development of the atomic bomb. However, Einstein was not involved in any way. Indeed, because of his public advocacy for anti-war and pacifist ideals, he was considered a dangerous figure and strictly excluded from the project.

In 1955, Albert Einstein died in New Jersey. The autopsy confirmed he died of heart failure, and his brain was removed and preserved in a laboratory for over 40 years. The story of this brain is documented in Michael Paterniti's famous book—"The Man Who Loved Books: The Story of the Brain of Albert Einstein."

[P4] 本页描绘了德国古城乌尔姆的全景，文字说明阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦于1879年3月14日在此诞生，并配有一个婴儿的哭声气泡。
[P5] 本页描述了爱因斯坦出生后家人对其外貌的担忧以及医生的安抚，随后讲述了他幼年语言发育迟缓，但三岁时首次说话便显露出聪明才智，对新出生的妹妹提出‘没有轮子’的童趣问题。
[P6] 本页描绘了幼年爱因斯坦脾气暴躁，对妹妹玛雅粗暴，甚至差点伤到她，而他的坏脾气也吓跑了家庭教师。
[P7] 本页展示了幼年爱因斯坦在专注时的两个场景：他能专注地叠起14层高的纸牌屋，同时对父亲送的指南针充满好奇，反复摆弄并思考其内部的秘密。
[P8] 爱因斯坦全家搬到慕尼黑后，父母为培养他的独立性，允许4岁的他独自上街，画面描绘了他站在繁忙街道上的场景。
[P9] 爱因斯坦开始上学，但因不喜欢运动，与喜欢踢球的同学们格格不入，被视为怪男孩。
[P10] 画面描绘了孩子们观看军人游行的场景，其他男孩兴奋不已，而爱因斯坦却显得不安，表现出他与众不同的性格和敏感内心。
[P11] 本页描绘了幼年爱因斯坦在学校因是唯一犹太人而遭受同学嘲笑和羞辱，同时他在学习上表现出对感兴趣科目专注、对不感兴趣科目懒散的特点，思考问题时反应较慢，引发老师对其智商的怀疑。
[P12] 本页讲述了12岁的爱因斯坦在学业上表现出色，尤其在数学方面天赋异禀。他通过阅读麦克斯·塔尔穆德赠送的几何学书籍，迅速掌握并深入研究更高阶的数学，展现出非凡的自学能力和热情。
[P13] 本页描绘了幼年爱因斯坦对枯燥教学的反感和对数学、音乐的热爱，他因态度冷漠被老师批评，但内心却在思考关于光速的深刻问题，展现出其独特的思维方式和对科学的早期探索。
[P14] 15岁的爱因斯坦因服兵役规定被迫留在德国，生活陷入低谷，后获准前往意大利与家人团聚，在温暖的家庭环境中重拾对数学的热爱，并在社交场合依然专注于思考。
[P15] 本页讲述了爱因斯坦未能直接进入苏黎世理工学院，后通过努力取得文凭并入学，毕业后在专利局工作，同时结婚生子，家庭生活并未影响他对科学问题的持续思考，他在日常生活中仍不断探索关于空间、时间、能量和物质的深刻问题。
[P16] 画面描绘了爱因斯坦推着婴儿车，背景是宇宙星系、原子模型、数学符号和公式E=mc²，象征科学与时间的交织，暗示他对物理和宇宙的深刻思考。
[P17] 本页通过文字和插图介绍了爱因斯坦的科学贡献，包括光电效应、相对论和E=mc²，并阐述了这些发现对科学界和日常生活的深远影响。同时，文字强调了爱因斯坦对名利的淡泊，以及他作为伟大思想家的最终形象。
[P18] 本页为作者后记，回顾了爱因斯坦的科学遗产、未因E=mc²获诺奖的真相、他与原子弹的关系，以及他去世后大脑被保存的轶事，强调了其思想的深远影响与历史误解。
[P19] 本页为书籍封底，展示了该书获得的奖项信息、ISBN编号及定价，背景插图为一个孩子在椅子上堆叠石块，周围环绕着几何图形和数学符号，象征探索与知识的积累。
